elements.label: EXAMPLE 3.14
elements.title: Polling organization survey results and probability calculation
elements.details:
| Description                          | Value |
|------------------------------------|-------|
| Sample size (number of people)     | 400   |
| Number in favor of increased funding | 312   |
| Probability of being in favor (P(A)) | 312/400 = 0.78 = 78% |
elements.summary: This example shows how to calculate the relative frequency probability of an event based on polling data, specifically the probability that a randomly selected person favors increased funding for local schools.

elements.label: EXAMPLE 3.15
elements.title: Medical knee surgery success probability calculation
elements.details:
| Description                          | Value |
|------------------------------------|-------|
| Number of knee surgeries performed | 200   |
| Number of successful surgeries     | 188   |
| Probability of success (P(A))       | 188/200 = 0.94 = 94% |
elements.summary: This example illustrates calculating the probability of success for knee surgery based on historical data of surgeries performed and their outcomes.
